marks.gloss_en: דילמא פחות מכביצה נטילה וברכה לא בעי, הא כביצה בעי נטילה וברכה (= p_pachot_lo_netila_uveracha, p_kebeitza_netila_uveracha): the egg-bulk threshold concerns washing and blessing, not the sukkah
the stam's inference from R' Tzadok's less-than-an-egg-bulk: an egg-bulk requires a sukkah
נאמר כאן חמשה עשר (Vayikra 23:34, Sukkot) ונאמר חמשה עשר בחג המצות (Vayikra 23:6): מה להלן לילה הראשון חובה מכאן ואילך רשות, אף כאן
R' Yochanan in R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak's name: the gezera shava ט"ו-ט"ו from the festival of matzot (= gs_chamisha_asar, p_ry_leil_rishon_chova)
R' Yochanan (in R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak's name): so here [Sukkot] the first night is obligatory, from then on optional
אי הכי, אפילו לילי יום טוב ראשון נמי! -- if the sukkah is like a dwelling where one eats at will, the first night too should be optional
R' Eliezer: a person is obligated to eat fourteen meals in the sukkah, one by day and one by night
R' Eliezer further: one who did not eat on the first festival night compensates on the last festival night
R' Eliezer's reason is the verse 'in sukkot you shall dwell (תשבו)'
and the Sages [what do they do with תשבו]? -- like a dwelling
and there, from where do we know? the verse says 'in the evening you shall eat matzot' (Shemot 12:18) -- Scripture fixed it as an obligation

והא אמר רבי אליעזר ארבע עשרה סעודות חייב אדם לאכול בסוכה, אחת ביום ואחת בלילה! -- R' Eliezer's compensation clause set against his own fourteen-meals statement (kind svara under protest: והא אמר has no ObjectionKind)
אמר בירא אמר רבי אמי: חזר בו רבי אליעזר -- R' Eliezer retracted (the fourteen-meals statement); = p_ami_chazar_bo
R' Ami: R' Eliezer retracted [his statement of fourteen meals]
תניא נמי הכי: אם השלים במיני תרגימא -- יצא
(entertained) with what does he compensate? -- say, with bread
the steward: for one like me, used to eat only one meal a day -- may I eat one meal and be exempt?
the steward: I have two wives and two sukkot, in Tiberias and in Tzippori -- may I go from sukkah to sukkah and be exempt?
